messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: compile-only in R?
parts:
Is it possible to compile a Stan model in R without running it and without needing to pass it data? I would find this convenient in applications where I'm running the same Stan model repeatedly: I could then compile it at the beginning with a simple function call, and then run the compiled version inside the loop.
A

messages.author: d4fb714af6c90658
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: compile-only in R?
parts:
It's easy.
Let's say that the model is in a "foo.stan" file:

A)
rt <- stanc("foo.stan", model_name = "foo")
foo.sm <- stan_model(stanc_ret = rt)

B)
foo.sm <- stan_model("foo.stan", model_name = "foo")

If your model is a string, such as

foo.string <- "
data { ... }
parameters { ... }
model { ... }
"

then:

A)
rt <- stanc(model_code = foo.string, model_name = "foo")
foo.sm <- stan_model(stanc_ret = rt)

B)
foo.sm <- stan_model(model_code = foo.string, model_name = "foo")

Sergio

messages.author: d4fb714af6c90658
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: compile-only in R?
parts:
A toy example:

betabin.string <- "
data {
    int N;
    int y[N];
}
parameters {
    real p;
}
model {
    p ~ beta(15, 2);
    y ~ bernoulli(p);
}
"
betabin.sm <- stan_model(model_code = betabin.string, model_name = "betabin")

p <- 0.3
times <- 50
prior <- rep(15/17,times)
posterior <- rep(NA, times)
true <- rep(p, times)
means <- data.frame(prior, posterior, true)
set.seed(12345)
for (i in 1:times) {
    N <- i * 10
    y <- rbinom(N, 1, p)
    sf <- sampling(betabin.sm, data = c("N", "y"), seed = 12345)
    means$posterior[i] <- mean(extract(sf)$p)
}
means[c(1,times),]

Output:

       prior posterior true
1  0.8823529 0.7787440  0.3
50 0.8823529 0.3086116  0.3

Sergio
